value.boilerplate: AstroDig LLC is an aerospace engineering company based in Boulder, Colorado. Founded in 2013, the company develops mission-analysis tools, robotic prospecting instruments, and controlled extraction test systems. Its long-term objective is an asteroid resource demonstration by 2032, subject to technical, financial, and mission-readiness gates.

sections.heading: Period and recognized source actuals
sections.text: USD; Q3 2024; period ended 2024-09-30. Revenue $9,490,000; COGS $3,606,200; opex $8,591,700; operating result $-2,707,900. Recognize engineering and development revenue against accepted contracted work; do not recognize projected asteroid sales.

sections.heading: Income reconciliation
sections.text:
Does recognized revenue cover delivery and operating costs?

Operating result remains negative after both delivery costs and development spending; the reconciliation isolates the reported loss rather than presenting revenue as profit.

sections.heading: Contracted service economics
sections.text:
How do the three service categories reconcile, and what share comes from engineering?

Recognized service categories reconcile to revenue. Engineering share describes the revenue base; no category-level profit is inferred because delivery costs are not allocated by service category.

sections.heading: Development spending intensity
sections.text:
How does research spending relate to revenue, workforce and total operating expense?

Research spending per period-end employee and relative to revenue exposes the development load. These ratios are descriptive; no capitalization, cash burn or return on investment is inferred.

sections.heading: Delivery capacity and evidence quality
sections.text:
How do delivered work and accepted or rejected trials relate to the workforce snapshot?

Completed work packages and reference acceptance are separate operating measures. Rejected trials remain in the denominator, and workforce ratios do not claim unused capacity.

sections.heading: Quarter-to-quarter operating bridge
sections.text:
Which recognized revenue and cost movements explain the change from Q2 to Q3?

The bridge reconciles revenue change, delivery-cost change and operating-expense change to the reported operating-result movement. It is an actual-period bridge, not a forecast or a causal attribution.

sections.heading: Backlog commitment scale
sections.text:
How large is remaining contracted work relative to current-quarter revenue and period-end headcount?

Backlog coverage and backlog per employee describe commitment scale at a point in time. They are not collection forecasts, cash balances, resource reserves or proof of available delivery capacity.

sections.heading: Methodology and limitations
sections.text: Freeze external interfaces only after verified supplier configuration evidence. Principal risk: supplier qualification. Flight-interface work is not a launch approval. Continue the approved ground-development scope; no asteroid commodity revenue is included in the operating outlook. No forecast, balance sheet, liquidity estimate, resource valuation, or cash-flow conclusion is supplied. Formula-linked analyses use recognized USD amounts and period-end operating snapshots; changing source inputs updates the calculations without changing the stated business scope.
